arxiv-2103-14616.title: Training a Task-Specific Image Reconstruction Loss
arxiv-2103-14616.creator: Aamir Mustafa, Aliaksei Mikhailiuk, Dan Andrei Iliescu, Rafał K. Mantiuk
arxiv-2103-14616.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Aamir Mustafa, Aliaksei Mikhailiuk, Dan Andrei Iliescu, Rafał K. Mantiuk. The choice of a loss function is an important factor when training neural networks for image restoration problems, such as single image super resolution. The loss function should encourage natural and perceptually pleasing results. A popular choice for a loss is a pre-trained network, such as VGG, which is used as a feature extractor for computing the difference between restored and reference images.

arxiv-2110-11156.title: DMS, AE, DAA: methods and applications of adaptive time series model selection, ensemble, and financial evaluation
arxiv-2110-11156.creator: Parley Ruogu Yang, Ryan Lucas
arxiv-2110-11156.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Parley Ruogu Yang, Ryan Lucas. Abstract We introduce three adaptive time series learning methods, called Dynamic Model Selection (DMS), Adaptive Ensemble (AE), and Dynamic Asset Allocation (DAA). The methods respectively handle model selection, ensembling, and contextual evaluation in financial time series. Empirically, we use the methods to forecast the returns of four key indices in the US market, incorporating information from the VIX and Yield curves. We present financial applications of the learning results, including fully-automated portfolios and dynamic hedging strategies.

arxiv-2307-15222.creator: Dipesh BHANDARI a and Michael CRESCIMANNO b
arxiv-2307-15222.description: Abstract Introducing a radially dependent magnetic field into Newton’s off-center circular orbits potential so as to preserve the E = 0 E=0 dynamical symmetry leads to a unique choice of field that can be identified as the inclusion of a magnetic monopole in the inverse stereographically projected problem.

arxiv-2401-03523.title: Characterizing Physical Memory Fragmentation
arxiv-2401-03523.creator: Mark Mansi, Michael M. Swift
arxiv-2401-03523.description: Abstract External fragmentation of physical memory occurs when adjacent differently sized regions of allocated physical memory are freed at different times, causing free memory to be physically discontiguous. It can significantly degrade system performance and efficiency, such as reducing the ability to use huge pages, a critical optimization on modern large-memory system.

arxiv-2502-07600.description: Abstract Predicting future scene representations is a crucial task for enabling robots to understand and interact with the environment. However, most existing methods rely on videos and simulations with precise action annotations, limiting their ability to leverage the large amount of available unlabeled video data.

arxiv-2503-03098.title: Quantum Magic in Quantum Electrodynamics
arxiv-2503-03098.creator: Qiaofeng Liu a , Ian Low a,b , and Zhewei Yin a,b
arxiv-2503-03098.description: Abstract In quantum computing, non-stabilizerness – the magic – refers to the computational advantage of certain quantum states over classical computers and is an essential ingredient for universal quantum computation. Employing the second order stabilizer Rényi entropy to quantify magic, we study the production of magic states in Quantum Electrodynamics (QED) via 2-to-2 scattering processes involving electrons and muons.

pmc-11470675.creator: Ting Wang, Lili Zhang, Wenxin Gao, Yidan Liu, Feng Yue, Xiaoling Ma, Lin Liu
pmc-11470675.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). N6-methyladenosine (m6A) is involved in most biological processes and actively participates in the regulation of reproduction. According to recent research, long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) and their m6A modifications are involved in reproductive diseases. In the present study, using m6A-modified RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing (m6A-seq), we established the m6A methylation transcription profiles in patients with recurrent implantation failure (RIF) for the first time. There were 1443 significantly upregulated m6A peaks and 425 significantly downregulated m6A peaks in RIF.

pmc-13400429.description: BackgroundThe introduction of consolidation durvalumab after chemoradiotherapy (CRT) for unresectable stage 3 non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), as established by the PACIFIC trial, has transformed survival outcomes. However, its impact remains uncertain in populations characterised by high levels of socioeconomic deprivation, multimorbidity, and historically poorer cancer outcomes compared to other regions.

pmc-13603556.title: Assessing Clinical Effectiveness of Ceftolozane/Tazobactam, Ceftazidime/Avibactam, and Meropenem/Vaborbactam in Bacteremia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-13603556.creator: Shahd Mohammad, Mosab Albalas, Mohammad M. Al-Ahmad
pmc-13603556.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background/Objectives: Bacteremia poses a significant clinical challenge, often necessitating the off-label use of novel β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor (BL/BLI) combinations such as Ceftolozane/Tazobactam (C/T), Ceftazidime/Avibactam (C/A), and Meropenem/Vaborbactam (M/V). Despite their widespread use, no conclusive data support their effectiveness in bacteremia. This meta-analysis aims to evaluate the clinical effectiveness of C/T, C/A, and M/V in treating bacteremia, with a focus on survival outcomes and clinical cure rates. Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted following a comprehensive search of Scopus and PubMed databases.

pmc-13625286.title: The potential role and research progress of the gut microbiota–NGF axis in postmenopausal bone homeostasis imbalance
pmc-13625286.creator: Yangyang Chen, Dingpeng Li, Zhong Wang, Jiawen Li, Haoze Zhang, Xingwen Xie
pmc-13625286.description: Postmenopausal osteoporosis(PMOP)is a common metabolic bone disease characterized by an imbalance in bone remodeling due to estrogen deficiency. Increasing evidence suggests that alterations in gut microbiota, intestinal barrier, immune response, microbial metabolites, and autonomic nervous activity are involved in postmenopausal bone loss.

pmc-13630473.title: The Dissemination of Standardised Care Protocol Guidelines for High‐Risk Emergency Abdominal Surgery Patients in Denmark
pmc-13630473.creator: Ines Victoria Føns Gjørup, Kim Wildgaard, Jakob Burcharth, Morten Vester‐Andersen
pmc-13630473.description: BackgroundPatients undergoing high‐risk emergency abdominal surgery have a high risk of postoperative complications and mortality. International studies suggest that standardised care protocol guidelines may improve outcomes, yet little is known about the dissemination of such guidelines in Denmark.MethodsWe conducted a nationwide cross‐sectional survey among Danish public hospitals treating high‐risk emergency abdominal surgical patients.
